'''Christian Serre''' (born 27 August 1970) is a French chemist and academic. He is a research director at the [[National Center for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) and the head of the Institute of Porous Materials of Paris.

Serre's research interests include the synthesis and applications of porous hybrid solids, such as [[metal-organic frameworks]]. He has received the CNRS [[Bronze Medal]], the Solid State Chemistry Award from the [[French Chemical Society]], and the Berthelot Medal from the [[French Academy of Sciences]]. He is also an elected member of the French Academy of Sciences.

==Education==
Serre earned an engineering degree from the [[École Supérieure de Physique et de Chimie Industrielles de la Ville de Paris]] (ESPCI) in 1994. He completed an [[M.Sc.]] in [[Physical Chemistry]] at [[Université Paris VI]] in 1995. In 1999, he received his [[Ph.D.]] in Materials Chemistry from the [[University of Versailles Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ens.psl.eu/sites/default/files/CV_Christian%20serre.pdf |title=Christian SERRE, 46 years old|website=École normale supérieure PSL|access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Serre's academic career includes his appointment as a CNRS research scientist at the [[Université de Versailles Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines]] from 2001 to 2009. He then became CNRS research director at the same institute from 2009 to 2016.<ref name=Chi/> In 2016, he established the Institute of Porous Materials of Paris at the École Normale Supérieure, [[ESPCI Paris]], the CNRS, and PSL University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chimie.ens.fr/recherche/laboratoire-imap/imap/?utm_source |title=Institute of Porous Materials (IMAP)
|website=Département de Chimie|access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> He also headed the Paris region priority project 'Respore' from 2017 to 2021<ref name=Chi>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chimie.ens.fr/recherche/laboratoire-imap/people/cserre/ |title=Christian Serre|website=Département de Chimie de|access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref> and has also been a director of the 'MaTerRE' Paris region priority project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dim-materre.fr/en/teams/ |title=Organisation|website=MaTerRE |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref> In 2021, he co-founded the startup Squair Tech.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://psl.eu/en/startup-des-laboratoires/squair-tech |title=Squair Tech|website=PSL University|access-date=October 29, 2025}}</ref>

==Research==
Serre's research has centered on the design and applications of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), to improve performance in advanced [[nanomaterials]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Bin |last2=Lu |first2=Feng-Fan |last3=Gu |first3=Xiao-Wen |last4=Shao |first4=Kai |last5=Wu |first5=Enyu |last6=Qian |first6=Guodong |title=Immobilization of Lewis Basic Nitrogen Sites into a Chemically Stable Metal-Organic Framework for Benchmark Water-Sorption-Driven Heat Allocations |journal=Advanced Science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) |date=2022 |volume=9 |issue=11 |page=3 |doi=10.1002/advs.202105556 |doi-access=free |pmid=35146963 |issn=2198-3844|pmc=9009103 }}</ref> with a focus on controlled structural modifications.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cej.2025.164016|title=Tuning ligand defect in porphyrins metal-organic frameworks to boost electrochemiluminescence for sensitive detection of amyloid-β1-42|first1=Jinyan|last1=Li|first2=Xiaoqi|last2=Pei|journal=Chemical Engineering Journal|volume=516|page=5|date=2025|article-number=164016 |doi=10.1016/j.cej.2025.164016|via=|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Serre worked on the synthesis of iron-, chromium- and aluminum based MIL series, demonstrating how typology control<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fu |first1=Jiarui |last2=Wu |first2=Yi-nan |title=A Showcase of Green Chemistry: Sustainable Synthetic Approach of Zirconium-Based MOF Materials |journal=Chemistry – A European Journal |date=2021 |volume=27 |issue=39 |page=9974 |doi=10.1002/chem.202005151 |pmid=33955075 }}</ref> and linker functionalization can be used to tune pore environments<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Highly Mesoporous Zr-Based MOF-Fabric Composites: A Benign Approach for Expeditious Degradation of Chemical Warfare Agents and Simulants|first1=Mai O|last1=Abdelmigeed|first2=John J|last2=Mahle|journal=Small|volume=20|issue=49|page=2|date=2024|doi=10.1002/smll.202405831 |pmid=39308233 |pmc=11618724 }}</ref> and generate large-pore, robust structures.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chempr.2023.09.005|title=Metal-organic frameworks for water vapor adsorption|first1=Le|last1=Shi|first2=Kent O.|last2=Kirlikovali|first3=Zhijie|last3=Chen|first4=Omar K.|last4=Farha|journal=Chem|volume=10|issue=2|page=488|date=2024|doi=10.1016/j.chempr.2023.09.005|bibcode=2024Chem...10..484S |osti=2294145 |via=Chem Journal}}</ref> He has also highlighted the scale-up<ref name=sca>{{cite journal |last1=Engel |first1=Emile R. |last2=Scott |first2=Janet L. |title=Advances in the green chemistry of coordination polymer materials |journal=Green Chemistry |date=2020 |volume=22 |issue=12 |page=3705 |doi=10.1039/D0GC01074J |language=en |issn=1463-9270|doi-access=free }}</ref> and development of “green” MOFs,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://ssrn.com/abstract=4606833|title=Some Metal-Organic Frameworks: from Green Synthesis to Applications - A mini-review|first1=Noura N.|last1=Eltahan|first2=Zeyad Y.|last2=Elbesh|first3=Abdulkarim A.|last3=Abdullah|first4=Mostafa M.|last4=Gaafar|journal=SSRN Electronic Journal|volume=|issue=|page=7|date=2023|doi=10.2139/ssrn.4606833|via=Damietta University - Faculty of Science}}</ref> for sustainable synthesis practices on MOF structure and performance.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1039/c9sc03916c|title=Improving MOF stability: approaches and applications|first1=Meili|last1=Ding|first2=Xuechao|last2=Cai|first3=Hai-Long|last3=Jiang|journal=Chemical Science|volume=10|issue=44|page=10213, 10217|date=2019|doi=10.1039/c9sc03916c|pmid=32206247 |via=RSC Publishing|pmc=7069376}}</ref>

Serre's research on robust scalable MOFs<ref name=rosc>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.solener.2024.112996|title=Material characteristics and selection criteria for adsorption-based atmospheric water harvesting: An overview|first1=Ibrahim I.|last1=El-Sharkawy|first2=Mohamed G.|last2=Gado|journal=Solar Energy|volume=283|page=10|date=2024|article-number=112996 |doi=10.1016/j.solener.2024.112996|bibcode=2024SoEn..28312996E |via=ScienceDirect|url-access=subscription}}</ref> has explored polymorphism, hydrophilicity,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.202304788|title=Water Adsorption in MOFs: Structures and Applications|first1=Bo|last1=Zhang|first2=Zerui|last2=Zhu|journal=Advanced Functional Materials|volume=34|issue=43|page=9|date=2023|doi=10.1002/adfm.202304788|via=Open Access|doi-access=free}}</ref> and water adsorption.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hastürk |first1=Emrah |last2=Höfert |first2=Simon-Patrick |last3=Topalli |first3=Burhan |last4=Schlüsener |first4=Carsten |last5=Janiak |first5=Christoph |title=Shaping of MOFs via freeze-casting method with hydrophilic polymers and their effect on textural properties |journal=Microporous and Mesoporous Materials |date=2020 |volume=295 |page=01 |article-number=109907 |doi=10.1016/j.micromeso.2019.109907 |bibcode=2020MicMM.29509907H |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1387181119307668 |issn=1387-1811|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In the area of nanomaterials, Serre has worked on biocompatible biodegradable MOF nanoparticles for imaging and targeted delivery<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US10738068B2/en?inventor=christian+serre&oq=christian+serre |title=Organic/inorganic hybrid nanoparticulates made from iron carboxylates|website=Google Patent|access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref> and has introduced synthesis routes that enabled uniform MOF nanoparticles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US20210277042A1/en |title=Low temperature process for the synthesis of MOF carboxylate nanoparticles|website=Google Patent|access-date=November 19, 2025}}</ref>
